thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Mostly Fall, Hit By Facebook's Premarket Dive

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Mostly Fall, Hit By Facebook's Premarket Dive
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Futures for the Dow inch higher, but those for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 are dropping
U.S. stock-index futures mostly pointed to a drop at the open Thursday, led lower by Facebook Inc.'s big premarket fall after its disappointing quarterly report.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
S&P 500 futures lost 4.80 points, or 0.2%, to 2,836.50, while those for the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 shed 61.25 points, or 0.8%, to 7,408.25.
Futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average , , which doesn't have Facebook as one of its components, bucked the negative trend, rising by 38 points, or 0.2%, to 25,441.
On Wednesday, the Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite finished higher, rallying into the close (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stock-futures-in-holding-pattern-as-analysts-brace-for-trump-juncker-fireworks-2018-07-25) after President Donald Trump and European Union chief Jean-Claude Juncker made a deal on trade (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-today-president-rips-cohen-over-tape-disclosure-defends-tariffs-2018-07-25).
The three gauges are showing year-to-date advances of 2.8% to 15%, as of Wednesday's close.
What's driving markets?
Facebook (FB)has been among the tech giants powering the stock market's gains (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tech-sector-contributed-all-of-the-stock-market-gains-so-far-in-2018-2018-07-02) this year, but the script just flipped. The social-media giant's shares were dropping 18% in premarket action after the company late Wednesday revealed lower-than-expected quarterly revenue, slowing user growth and weak guidance (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-stock-crushed-after-revenue-user-growth-miss-2018-07-25).
Outside of Facebook-related gloom, European stocks on Thursday were cheering Wednesday's upbeat meeting between Trump and the European Commission's president. The two leaders reached a trade agreement that has been called short on specifics, but still significant. The deal shows the White House is willing to at least consider not letting global trade tensions spiral out of control, said a MarketWatch column (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/even-if-short-of-specifics-the-trump-juncker-agreement-is-significant-2018-07-25).
What are strategists saying?
"Facebook is expected to see its biggest one-day selloff when it opens later today. The big question will be whether it will bring down the rest of the FAANG stocks," said Jasper Lawler, head of research at London Capital Group, in a note, referring to Facebook, Apple Inc. (AAPL) , Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) , Netflix Inc. (NFLX)and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOGL) .
"Whilst we expect Facebook's results have a short-term impact on FAANG stocks, it's more likely that we will start to see a de-coupling of Facebook from the group," Lawler added.
